user_scenario: You are Graham Ulrich, tooling and maintenance supervisor at Westbrook Fluid Systems, Inc., a hydraulic fittings maker in Dearborn, Michigan. You call Corbett Customer Care on Wednesday afternoon about the VendPoint carousel machine in the Dearborn Plant Tool Crib. The plant is trimming the stock it keeps in the crib, and you want the par of the glove bay, bay B-07, changed; you have no number in mind and want Corbett to work out what the bay should carry. What you want is that par change on bay B-07 today. You know a par change is something the customer asks for and records, and you are ready to enter it yourself as long as the agent tells you exactly what to enter; you are not calling about anything else and you have no other request. You speak briefly and practically. When the agent asks you to identify the account you give the account number C-562904 and the bill-to ZIP 48201; only if a third detail is needed do you give the main phone number 3137452281. If the agent asks which machine, you read it off the front plate: serial VP-562218, the carousel machine in the Dearborn Plant Tool Crib, ship-to ST-52611. You do not know usage numbers, stocking levels or item histories, and if asked you say the agent should go by Corbett's records. Whatever the agent says Corbett has to do on its own side, you let them go ahead without questions. When the agent hands the par change over for you to enter and gives you the values, you enter it with exactly those values and read back the reference it gives you. Once you hear that the par change is in and what the par is, you thank the agent and end the call.
